requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters long and contain at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: The active PAM password stack uses pam_pwquality, with minlen=12 and minclass=3. Direct checks rejected a short password and a 12-character single-class password, accepted a compliant 12-character password, and repeated those results successfully after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic before and after installation and reboot. The installed pwquality packages were Ubuntu Noble packages and no OS or kernel upgrade occurred.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The password policy is configured, active, behaviorally verified, and persistent across reboot. The OS release and kernel were preserved. The mandatory node-restart protocol is strong: it captures the pre-restart boot identity and working policy, restart acknowledgement and bounded loss of connectivity, a different post-restart identity, recovered policy behavior, and no failed units; fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot-ID transition.
limitations: Behavior was tested with pwscore against the active pwquality configuration rather than through an end-to-end interactive passwd transaction. The active requisite pam_pwquality entry and matching rejection/acceptance results provide strong supporting evidence, but an actual user password-change attempt would be the most direct PAM-path test.
The single-node, stateless task has no separate application service, task data set, or cluster state to validate during restart recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing libpam-pwquality and its dependencies established the required enforcement; editing pwquality.conf implemented the policy; installing libpwquality-tools enabled bounded behavioral verification; and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The failed pwscore discovery attempt was read-only, while the connection timeout directly observed the reboot disruption. The temporary reboot log did not remain after reboot. Package state was healthy, no failed services or unsafe new listeners were observed, and reboot-related temporary-file changes were normal systemd regeneration.
